chief_complaint: Pregnancy with uncontrolled hypertension, chronic low back pain on opioid therapy, and anemia
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 47-year-old woman who became pregnant on 2022-12-30. Since the start of pregnancy she has stage 2 hypertension (BP 149/98 mmHg) and chronic anemia diagnosed in 2010. She has a history of prediabetes (A1c 6.1%) and longstanding chronic low back pain managed with ibuprofen and a Percocet combination. Stress, social isolation, limited social contact, part‑time employment and a criminal record are documented, contributing to psychosocial strain. A medication review flag has been active since 2020, and current medications include lisinopril, ibuprofen, and Percocet, none of which have documented pregnancy‑safe indications. Routine labs such as BMI, lipid profile, and eGFR are missing. The patient has had frequent outpatient and wellness visits but limited acute care encounters.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include gingivitis (most recent resolution 2022-04-15), a lost dental filling, prior resolved stress and medication review flags, two concussions resolved in 2019, viral sinusitis episodes resolved in 2017 and 2019, a prior normal pregnancy that ended in miscarriage in 2000, and a miscarriage history. These reflect a background of dental disease, minor head trauma, and prior obstetric loss.

active_medications.name: Acetaminophen 325 MG / Oxycodone Hydrochloride 10 MG Oral Tablet (Percocet)

social_determinants: Part‑time employment, criminal record, limited social contact, social isolation, chronic stress, and higher education. These factors may affect health‑care access, medication adherence, and prenatal care utilization.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 149/98 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension), A1c 6.1% (prediabetic), chronic anemia, no BMI, lipid panel, or eGFR available. Charlson index 1, clinical complexity moderate. Pregnancy amplifies cardiovascular, metabolic, and medication safety risks. Opioid use and NSAID therapy add renal and fetal concerns. Psychosocial stressors increase risk for poor prenatal outcomes.

data_quality_flags.issue: Missing latest BMI; obesity status unknown.
Total cholesterol and LDL values are missing; ASCVD risk cannot be calculated.
Renal function not documented; important given ACE‑inhibitor use.
Purpose for each medication is unspecified in the record.
No prenatal ultrasound or related imaging documented.
Hypertension not listed as an active condition despite elevated BP readings.

clinical_impression: A pregnant woman with multiple high‑risk comorbidities: uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension, chronic anemia, prediabetes, and chronic low back pain managed with NSAIDs and opioids. Medication safety concerns (ACE‑inhibitor, NSAID, opioid) are prominent. Psychosocial stressors and limited social support further increase risk for adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Gaps in key laboratory data and medication indication documentation limit comprehensive risk assessment.
